hook: A small science lab full of equipment to find: tap each object in the picture, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt in a small, slightly cluttered science laboratory with 32 things to find, every one a noun you meet when people talk about research and experiments — der Bunsenbrenner in the fume hood, das Stativ with its funnel, die Zentrifuge by the sink, das Fossil on the shelf. The prompt asks Wo ist der Erlenmeyerkolben? and you tap it in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Erlenmeyerkolben?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. A tap on bare wall costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. No object is asked twice in the same run.
tips[0].title: Compounds in the lab: the last part decides
tips[0].text: Lab words are long, but the last part decides the article. Reagenzglas + Ständer: der Ständer, so der Reagenzglasständer. Gas + Flasche: die Flasche, so die Gasflasche — and die Tropfflasche too. Read to the end of the word before you choose.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is der Ständer, so the whole word is der Reagenzglasständer — even though das Reagenzglas comes first.
tips[1].title: Tools in -er are masculine — but not das Fenster
tips[1].text: A thing that does a job, named with -er, is masculine: der Bunsenbrenner, der Feuerlöscher, der Trichter, der Hocker. Not every word ending in -er is a tool, though: das Fenster is neuter, and so is das Waschbecken, which only sounds similar.
tips[1].check.why: Brenner is a device that burns, built on brennen + -er, so it is der Bunsenbrenner.
tips[2].title: Foreign lab words: listen to the ending
tips[2].text: Many science words come from Latin, Greek or French, and their endings carry the gender. -ie, -ette and -uge are feminine: die Batterie, die Pinzette, die Zentrifuge. -ium, -op, -iv and -il are neuter: das Aquarium, das Teleskop, das Stativ, das Fossil.
tips[2].check.why: Words ending in -uge, like die Zentrifuge, are feminine.
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: das Reagenzglas + der Ständer → der Reagenzglasständer.
remember[1]: -er devices are der (der Bunsenbrenner, der Feuerlöscher), but das Fenster is neuter.
